Table.caption: Table S33. Genes intersecting XtX outlier SNPs, ordered by maximum XtX (results/outlier_genes.csv, results/outliers_annotated.txt). Table.label: S35
Table.caption: Table S35. Full residue spectrum of the 24 polymorphic codons, by agro-ecological zone, with Wilson 95 per cent confidence intervals (results/codon_panel_residues.csv). Rows are codon–residue pairs; † marks the 3D7 reference residue, which is reported explicitly because at pfdhps 437 the reference residue is the resistance allele (Section 6.9.4) and because at seven of the 24 codons the non-reference residue is the majority one: pfdhfr 51 (Ile 0.786), pfdhfr 59 (Arg 0.886), pfdhfr 108 (Asn 0.908), pfdhps 436 (Ala 0.541), pfmdr1 184 (Phe 0.677), pfmdr2 492 (Val 0.549) and pfaat1 258 (Leu 0.609). Residues within a codon are ordered by overall frequency; the 33 codons fixed at the reference residue are omitted — the 22 pfk13 ones are listed in Table S38, and the remaining 11 (pfcrt 72 and 73, pfmdr1 1034 and 1042, pfdhfr 16 and 164, pfmdr2 484, pfcoronin 50, 100 and 107, and pfaat1 313) appear only in the source file. Overall denominators are per codon and run 1,858–1,900 of 1,900 isolates across the 24 codons shown; the panel-wide range of 1,834–1,900 quoted in Section 6.9.2 includes fixed codons omitted here, its lower bound being pfmdr1 1034. χ² p tests heterogeneity of that residue against all other residues at the same codon across the four zones, so a codon with four residues yields four tests whose p-values differ — pfdhps 436 is the only such codon. Zone column headings are spelled correctly here for display; the source geospatial layer and the source columns of codon_panel_residues.csv read Decidous_forest and Transitional_zone, and the spatial join keys on that source spelling (see Methods).

Table.label: S44
Table.caption: Table S44. Threshold sensitivity. Every isolate resolves to one of seven administrative-level-1 coordinates (black points), which is the entire spatial resolution available to this analysis.
